previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted after accidental dislodgement of his tunneled Remodulin catheter while showering. He developed febrile neutropenia on hospital day 2 with a white blood cell count of 0.7 and ANC of 234, likely due to recent gastroenteritis from consuming rancid butter. He was treated with vancomycin and Zosyn for 3 days, remained afebrile after day 3, and blood cultures were negative. A new tunneled central line was placed on hospital day 4 after platelet transfusion and confirmation of no active infection. His portopulmonary hypertension remained stable on Remodulin 45 ng/kg/min and sildenafil, with no change in oxygen requirements. Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia were managed with supplementation, and magnesium oxide was increased to 800 mg daily. He was discharged home with outpatient follow-up in hematology, pulmonology, and hepatology, and instructions to monitor weight and catheter site.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ Year old male with HCV cirrhosis (complicated by HE, varices, 
ascites), hepatopulmonary syndrome on chronic Remodulin infusion 
therapy, listed for transplant, presented with 5 days of diffuse 
abdominal pain and rebound tenderness on exam, with CT showing 
bowel wall edema.

# Abdominal pain: Non specific colitis. Paitent presented with a 
week of cramping abdominal pain and increased wateriness of 
chornic lactulose/remodulin-induced diarrhea, along with low 
grade fevers. On exam patient had rebound tenderness in the 
lower quadrants and stable splenomegaly. He had no leukocytosis 
or acute LFT abnormalities, blood and urine cultures were 
negative to date and CT abdomen with contrast showed hepatic 
flexure colitis. Stool c. diff study was negative, stool 
cultures were pending at time of discharge. Could not perform 
diagnostic paracentesis given lack of ascitic fluid amenable to 
paracentesis on ultrasound.  Transplant surgery was consulted 
and did not recommend surgical intervention. Patient was first 
started on piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin out of concern 
for febrile neutropenia in patient with central venous 
cathether. Vancomycin was discontinued and patient was able to 
be discharged on ciprofloxacin and metronidazole when ANC 
remained >1000 as empiric treatment for non-specific colitis in 
non-neutropenic patient.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION: ___ year old man with cirrhosis/Hep C, neutropenia, portopulmonary
hypertension and splenic enlargement, on Remodulin for pulmonary hypertension;
generalized tenderness to percussion on exam; evaluate for source of possible
peritonitis; evaluate for ascites, comment if present on whether further
imaging would be needed to tap 

COMPARISON:  CT from ___ and MR ___ & L spine ___

TECHNIQUE: CT Abdomen and Pelvis with 100 cc of Omnipaque 350. Multiplanar
reformated images were obtained. Oral contrast was administered.

FINDINGS:

CT ABDOMEN:
Mild bibasilar subsegmental atelectasis. Normal visualized heart without
significant pericardial effusion.

Trace to mild amount of ascites is noted most prominently in the perihepatic
and perisplenic regions. Significant hazy mesenteric stranding is scattered
throughout the abdomen but resides predominantly about the right upper
quadrant, specifically about the hepatic flexure of the colon. This may
represent ascitic fluid versus underlying inflammatory changes.

The liver demonstrates nodular contour without focal lesion. Atrophic
pancreas. Small hypodense lesion in the superior pole of the right kidney,
incompletely characterized but could be further evaluated with non-urgent
ultrasound. The gallbladder, both adrenals and remainer of thekidneys are
normal. 

Marked sequela of portal hypertension with marked splenomegaly (measuring 20
cm in CC dimension) and significant gastro-splenic varices. The largest
caliber of these varices measures up to 4 cm in width. Smaller caliber distal
paraesophageal varices are also noted.

Notable bowel wall thickening involving the hepatic flexure of the colon with
surrounding fluid as described above. Similar milder finding is noted about
the sigmoid colon. The remainder of the small bowel and colon appear
relatively normal. No free is noted. 

CT PELVIS: Mild to moderate amount of low density ascites is also noted to the
lower pelvis. Urinary bladder is distended without wall thickening.

BONES: Lower lumbar spine posterior spinal fusion changes and vertebroplasty
changes at multiple levels in the lumbar spine. Multilevel vertebral body
height loss involving T7, T9, T11-L4 vertebral bodies of varying height loss
all relatively stable since ___ MRI T and L spine comparison.

IMPRESSION:

1. Hepatic flexure colonic wall thickening and nonspecific surrounding fluid
and mesenteric haziness with background ascites. This may represent an
underlying colitis, specifically pseudomembranous colitis, given history of
antibiotics and recent hospitalization as discussed with Dr. ___. 

2. Marked sequelae of cirrhosis and portal venous hypertension with
significant gastro-splenic varices and smaller caliber distal paraesophageal
varices. Atrophic pancreas is also noted.

3. Small hypodense lesion in the superior pole of the right kidney,
incompletely characterized but could be further evaluated with non-urgent
ultrasound. 

4. Multilevel vertebral body height loss.
